title: enbrief(mechanic): a rejects.toThrow clamp has no teeth when the swallowed path throws downstream anyway
description:
## .what

a regression clamp for a failhide repair that asserts .rejects.toThrow() can have no teeth: when the swallowed fault is followed by a second operation that hits the same bad state, the defect still throws, from a different site.

evidence: a findsert of a fixed-content .gitignore swallowed every read error via .catch(() => null); the repair rethrew non-ENOENT errors. the clamp put a directory at the target path and asserted .rejects.toThrow(). with the repair reverted, the clamp stayed green: readFile(dir) -> EISDIR -> null, then writeFile(dir) -> EISDIR throws anyway. both arms throw, so the assertion could not tell them apart. it was found only via the revert-the-fix dogfood step of rule.require.clamp-edge-cases.

the same shape recurs wherever a swallowed fault is followed by a downstream op on the same state: rethrow a read error (the write throws), rethrow a parse error (the consumer that dereferences throws), rethrow a lookup error (the caller that asserts presence throws).

## .why

a toThrow assertion tests the EXISTENCE of a throw; a failhide repair is a claim about its ORIGIN. the loose form cannot express the second, so the clamp reads as protection and guards naught. a whole-error snapshot can bite, but only by accident of which fields it records.

## .shape of the fix

a brief under code.test/pitofsuccess.errors/, beside rule.forbid.failhide and rule.require.failloud (and cross-linked from rule.require.clamp-edge-cases):

- the test: if the defect were present, would this assertion still pass? for a throw: would a DIFFERENT throw, from a different site, satisfy it?
- the rule: a clamp on a rethrow asserts WHICH fault propagated, never THAT one did. name the field that parts them, e.g. expect(error.code).toEqual(EISDIR) plus expect(error.syscall).toEqual(read), not open
- blocker: a bare .rejects.toThrow() as the sole clamp on a failhide repair where a downstream op on the same state also throws

related, not duplicates: #656, #655, #651 (clamp teeth in other shapes).
